data.title: Biggest stock movers Tuesday: PLAY, ENVA, and more
data.description:
Stock futures inched lower Tuesday morning as Middle East supply risks, high bond yields, and calls for a deliberate pause in AI development weigh on sentiment ahead of the Fed rate decision.

Here are some of Tuesday's biggest stock movers:

Biggest stock gainers

  • Radiant Logistics (RLGT) +13% - Shares jumped after the logistics company reported strong FQ4 results with revenue rising 18.6% Y/Y. Adjusted net income increased 34.5% to $7.4M, while adjusted EBITDA rose 31.6% to $10.4M, and the adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 240 basis points to 15.5%. Gross profit increased 11.2% to $64.4M, with strength in U.S. forwarding operations and international airfreight. Radiant also amended its $200M revolving credit facility, extending maturity to 2031 and increasing its acquisition-focused accordion to $100M. The company entered fiscal 2027 with no net debt.

Biggest stock losers

  • Enova International (ENVA) -20% - Shares tumbled after the financial services company withdrew its applications with the OCC and Federal Reserve related to its proposed acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp. Enova said the decision followed a thorough evaluation of the regulatory process, while CEO Steve Cunningham said the company did not believe regulatory guidelines provided clear standards for nonbanks seeking to become banks. The company reaffirmed its Q3 outlook for revenue growth of around 25% and adjusted EPS growth of around 30% Y/Y, along with FY2026 revenue growth of 20%-25% and adjusted EPS growth of 30%-35%. Enova also said it plans to accelerate share repurchases through the remainder of 2026, with $349M available under its current board authorization as of June 30.
  • Dave & Buster's Entertainment (PLAY) -14% - Shares plunged after higher food and beverage, payroll, and pre-opening costs pushed the entertainment and restaurant operator to an unexpected Q2 loss. Adjusted EPS came in at -$0.27, missing the $0.19 consensus and reversing from a $0.40 profit a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA fell to $98.9M from $129.8M and missed the $118.8M estimate. Revenue declined 2.4% Y/Y, as comparable-store sales weakened and entertainment revenue declined. Food and beverage costs rose 11%, entertainment costs 5%, and payroll costs 1%, pushing total operating expenses up 4%.

  • Sysco (SYY) -2% - Shares fell after the foodservice distributor priced an offering of about 12.34M common shares at $81 each, with gross proceeds of roughly $1B. Sysco expects the offering to close September 16 and plans to use the net proceeds to finance part of the consideration for its pending acquisition of Jetro Restaurant Depot. Underwriters also have a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional $150M of shares at the same price to cover potential overallotments.

data.title: U.S. has weapons in space, Air Force secretary confirms
data.description:
The U.S. military has confirmed that it deployed weapons in space, the first public acknowledgment of such capabilities, in what is considered a warning to China and Russia. 

"We are increasing readiness against existing threats, and the United States has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action," Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference in Maryland on Monday.

"It is critically important that we maintain our dominance not only in the air but in space, and so we've had to take steps to make sure that when we're threatened, we can take care of that," he said. "We're not going to talk about the specifics of what we're doing, whether we've tested, not tested, or anything else."

However, Meink did mention the Space-Based Interceptor program, "which moved from initial contract to flight-ready hardware in less than one year." The program is a key feature of the Golden Dome initiative.

"We are making similar progress in our Space Data Network, and we start launching our Air Moving Target Indication constellation this month," he added.

A Space Force spokesperson said U.S. space capabilities can be employed for offensive and defensive purposes.

"The U.S. has warned about Russian and Chinese weapons testing and operationalization since 2007," the spokesperson said. "Due to their actions, it is no longer a question that space is a warfighting domain. Open communication strengthens deterrence, prevents adversary miscalculation, and normalizes space operations alongside the other services."

data.title: European stocks slide as oil tops $107, bond yields climb
data.description:
London (UKX) -0.94%; the UK's unemployment holds at 4.9%.

Germany (DAX:IND) -0.96%, the lowest since July 24 and marking the second day of losses, led by banks.

France (CAC:IND) -0.98%. France's inflation accelerates to 2.4% in August.

In other parts of Europe, Slovakia's annual inflation rate eased to 3.1% in August.

The annual inflation rate in Poland rose to 3.4% in August.

Spain’s annual inflation rate rose to 4.3% in August.

Industrial production in Hungary increased 4.7% Y/Y in July.

The pan-European Stoxx 600 (STOXX) edged 0.96% lower to 629.9 to three-month lows, as oil prices continued to climb, with Brent crude trading above $107 a barrel, adding to concerns over an already challenging inflation outlook. Bond yields also continued to rise, reaching multi-year highs and further weighing on equity valuations and investor sentiment.

In the bond market, the U.S. bond was up 8 basis points to 5.04%.

UK's 10-year yield was up 6 basis points to 5.43%. 

Germany's 10-year yield was up 4 basis points to 3.57%. 

Currencies: (EUR:USD) (GBP:USD) (CHF:USD)

data.title: J&J reports phase 2b data on less-frequent lung cancer treatment
data.description:
• Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) reported new Phase 2b COPERNICUS study results showing that less-frequent dosing and preventive strategies with RYBREVANT FASPRO and LAZCLUZE could improve the treatment experience for patients with previously untreated advanced non-small cell lung cancer carrying common EGFR mutations.
  • Low rates of rash, blood clots, and administration-related reactions were observed with subcutaneous treatment and prophylaxis, the company said.
  • Fewer than 1% of patients discontinued treatment due to treatment-related events at one year.
  • New findings from Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) build on the MARIPOSA survival benefit and strengthen evidence for RYBREVANT FASPRO plus LAZCLUZE as first-line treatment.

data.title: Stock futures slide as 10-year Treasury yield tops 5% ahead of Fed decision
data.description:
Stock index futures were lower on Tuesday while Treasury yields rose as traders looked forward to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision later in the week.

Dow futures (INDU) -0.68%, S&P 500 futures (SPX) -0.50%, and Nasdaq futures (US100:IND) -0.53%.

The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades, extending a global bond selloff driven by surging energy prices, rising debt, and inflation concerns.

The bond-market selloff adds pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision Wednesday, with investors expecting officials to raise short-term borrowing costs for the first time since July 2023.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 1.8 basis points to 4.69%, the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) rose 5.4 basis points to 5.04%, and the 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) rose 4.7 basis points to 5.40%.

On the economic calendar, investors will monitor the Empire State Manufacturing Index and the 20-yr Bond Auction.

Among S&P 500 stocks, Keysight Technologies (KEYS) +1.78%, Nasdaq (NDAQ) +1.56%, Coherent (COHR) +1.54%, Genuine Parts (GPC) +1.49%, and Flex (FLEX) +1.43%.

Sysco (SYY) -2.18%, Coinbase Global (COIN) -2.04%, Brown & Brown (BRO) -1.75%, Healthpeak Properties (DOC) -1.61%, and Republic Services (RSG) -1.51%.

data.title: Borr Drilling to sell 51% stake in two Mexican joint ventures
data.description:
• Borr Drilling (BORR) has agreed to sell its 51% stake in two Mexican joint ventures to its long-standing local partner in the country.
  • Upon completion of the transaction, Borr Drilling will have fully divested Perfomex, while its local partner will become the sole owner of Perfomex and assume responsibility for the management and operation of the company's jack-up rigs Galar, Gersemi and Njord, which are currently operating with PEMEX.
  • The company will retain ownership of the three rigs and continue participating in the underlying contracts through bareboat charter agreements, with economics expected to be largely unchanged from the existing arrangement.
  • Njord is currently contracted through April 2028, with extension options thereafter, while Galar and Gersemi are contracted through May 2030.
  • Following completion of the transaction, Perfomex will continue its operations related to integrated well services and PEMEX, while Borr Drilling will independently operate and market its fleet to other operators in the region through its affiliated companies.
  • The transaction is expected to simplify Borr Drilling's corporate and operating structure in Mexico.
